image_description: A close-up shot of a black hockey puck resting on the white, curved boards of an ice hockey rink. The puck is positioned in the lower-left quadrant. The background shows the glossy, slightly worn surface of the rink boards with some branding text visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact solid disk with diameter moderately exceeding its thickness, creating a stout cylindrical profile.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly exhibits the standard 3:1 diameter-to-thickness ratio characteristic of a hockey puck.
The object appears solid and opaque with sharp edges, consistent with a hard rubber disk.
The surface is highly reflective and glossy, showing strong specular highlights, rather than the expected matte finish of vulcanized rubber.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The puck exhibits a plastic-like, high-gloss sheen with sharp specular highlights. Real hockey pucks are matte black vulcanized rubber. This suggests a material rendering error common in AI generation where 'black object' defaults to shiny plastic/metal.

The shadow under the puck is soft and diffuse, but the contact edge lacks a precise occlusion line. The puck seems to float slightly above the board rather than resting heavily on it, indicating minor grounding issues.
There is text on the black strip of the rink board ('R...'). It is partially legible but lacks the crispness of real printed vinyl, appearing slightly melted or inconsistent in font weight.
